descriptionChirho: Adjective describing physical constriction or insufficiency of space: narrow, tight, cramped, small. Used of a narrow place (Num 22:26 makom tsar), a space too cramped for the sons of the prophets (2 Kgs 6:1), a tight seal (Job 41:15), a narrow pit like a harlot (Prov 23:27), and feeble strength (Prov 24:10). Consistently rendered Arabic dayyiq (ضَيِّق), Korean jop-eun (좁은), Spanish estrecho/apretado, Hindi tang (तंग) or sankirn (संकीर्ण). The semantic core is physical restriction or limitation of dimensions, distinct from the homonymous II. tsar meaning adversary/enemy.

Substantivized participle or adjective used as a noun meaning adversary, opponent, or enemy. In Isa 59:19 the tsar is one who oppresses or attacks, rendered German Bedraenger (oppressor), Hindi shatru (शत्रु, enemy), Korean jo-eun (좋은, contextually hostile one), Spanish angosto (metaphorical narrowing/constriction). This sense overlaps with II. tsar (H6862b) and may represent a borderline case between the physical 'narrow/constricting' adjective and the personal noun 'adversary' -- the one who constricts or presses upon another.
